title: Architecture routing and failure lab
description: Compare component choices and failure states. The paths describe product design consequences, not measured InternVL3 checkpoint behavior.

visionOptions.label: Detail-preserving vision encoder
visionOptions.detail: Retains more local evidence for dense pages and small controls.
visionOptions.capability: Best chance of preserving dense visual evidence

visionOptions.label: Compact vision encoder
visionOptions.detail: Uses fewer features for faster, lower-cost requests.
visionOptions.capability: Good for coarse scene and large-object tasks
visionOptions.latency: Lower encoder work; fine detail can be lost

projectorOptions.label: Trained multimodal projector
projectorOptions.detail: Maps ordered visual features into the language model input contract.
projectorOptions.capability: Can bind language to visual regions
projectorOptions.risk: Requires versioned compatibility with both model sides

projectorOptions.label: Aggressive pooled projector
projectorOptions.detail: Reduces visual tokens by summarizing regions before fusion.

languageOptions.label: Reasoning language model
languageOptions.detail: Uses a larger decode budget for multi-step explanation.
languageOptions.capability: Better fit for synthesis and cross-image reasoning
languageOptions.risk: Decoder latency and output cost dominate

languageOptions.label: Fast task model
languageOptions.detail: Optimized for extraction, routing, and short constrained outputs.
languageOptions.risk: Less headroom for long, ambiguous reasoning

failureOptions.label: Media decode rejected
failureOptions.detail: The input is malformed or exceeds an upload policy.

failureOptions.label: Vision worker unavailable
failureOptions.detail: The visual encoder cannot accept work.

failureOptions.label: Projector compatibility failure
failureOptions.detail: Feature shape or model-version validation fails.

failureOptions.label: Language-model deadline exceeded
failureOptions.detail: The decoder misses its response budget.
